transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Halia), Samir Patel (Halia), Ruth Kim (Halia), Omar Hassan (Halia)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing, shortlist of open models for the POC (multilingual/multi-domain needs), benchmark plan and timelines. Halia is a biotech/therapeutics product team that wants a small pilot to evaluate feasibility of model-assisted literature synthesis and multi-lingual triage. They prefer open models for cost and control. Security/compliance (SOC2, VPC, KMS) are deal blockers.

Topics:
- Success criteria (quality metrics, latency, cost targets)
- Workload sizing (QPS, avg tokens, peak concurrency)
- Benchmark plan (datasets, evals, pass/fail thresholds)
- Model shortlist and tradeoffs (Llama2, Mistral, Falcon, RedPajama variants)
- Timeline and next steps for a 4-6 week POC

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight. quick intros please.
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here, head of ML at Halia—focusing on knowledge extraction from papers.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, platform eng, I own infra and deployments.
[00:16] Ruth Kim: Ruth, security/compliance.
[00:19] Omar Hassan: Omar, product.
[00:21] Maya Chen: Great. Diego and Priya from our SE team here to cover perf and model stuff, and I'll own next steps and pricing.

[00:30] Diego Ramos: Quick agenda — confirm success criteria, get workload numbers, propose shortlist of open models, outline benchmarks and timeline.
[00:39] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. High level: we want automated literature summaries and triage in English, Spanish, and German. Domain is biomedical — high precision required for entity extraction and claims. Must have low hallucination on citations.

[01:02] Samir Patel: For throughput, normal load is about 30 concurrent users, expect 2 calls per user per minute at peak, so roughly 60 rps peak. Avg prompt + response length around 512 tokens, with some long runs up to 2k tokens for full-article synth. Latency SLO — ideally <700ms for standard synth flows, but we know that's tough for long sequences.

[01:35] Diego Ramos: OK that helps. For the POC we usually recommend restricting to shorter outputs initially to hit latency targets. We'll size test clusters for both short (<=512 tokens) and long (up to 2k) flows.

[02:02] Priya Nair: On quality, what threshold would you consider success? F1 for entity extraction? Or human eval?
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: Mix — automated metrics (exact match/F1 on a labeled dev set) plus a human quality score. For the POC, target is >=0.78 F1 on extraction and human preference >=60% vs our current baseline (rule-based). Also hallucination rate under 5% on a citation-check set.

[02:40] Maya Chen: Good clear targets. Now model shortlist — we suggested open models due to cost and ability to run in Dedicated/Private later. Thoughts?

[02:52] Omar Hassan: Open models are preferred, yes. Also we might need on-prem later for patient data.

[03:05] Diego Ramos: Proposed shortlist: Llama-2 13B (refined instruction-tuned), Mistral 7B Instruct, Falcon 40B Instruct, and a RedPajama/Redwood-verified 13B variant. We'll also include a quantized 13B 4-bit profile to test cost/latency tradeoffs.

[03:28] Samir Patel: Any domain-adapted weights available? Medical fine-tuned?

[03:33] Priya Nair: There are medical fine-tunes for some models but often not open-source or licensed. For the POC we recommend using base open models with instruction-tuning plus a lightweight retrieval/RAG layer and domain prompts. If that falls short we can explore small domain fine-tunes (100-500M steps) in a later phase.

[03:58] Lena Ortiz: Multilingual performance is a concern — Mistral reportedly weaker in German, Llama2 better but larger. How do we pick?

[04:10] Diego Ramos: We'll run a small multilingual eval set — English/Spanish/German samples from your corpus. For POC we'll test each candidate on that set and report BLEU/rouge/F1 plus human assessment. We'll surface per-language errors so you can see tradeoffs.

[04:33] Maya Chen: Cost targets? What is acceptable for you per 1k tokens or per inference?

[04:38] Samir Patel: For pilot, we're aiming to be conservative — prefer cost under $0.02 per 1k tokens delivered (hosted equivalent) so we can scale in prod. But we mostly care about total monthly cost projection given expected usage.

[04:55] Diego Ramos: Ok our Optimize toolkit can produce cost estimates for the different quant/profile combos — we'll include that in the POC report. Quantized 4-bit can drop cost a lot, sometimes by 2-3x, with some quality tradeoff but often acceptable for extraction tasks.

[05:18] Ruth Kim: Security questions up front: do you provide VPC/private deployment? How do you handle KMS, audit logs, and data retention? We need SOC2 evidence.

[05:30] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private provides customer-managed VPC or on-prem. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, and we emit audit logs for every request. We'll send the SOC2/ISO pack. For the POC we can run on a dedicated sandbox in your cloud with KMS integration.

[05:50] Ruth Kim: Good. Also need per-token logging control and ability to disable retention for patient-related prompts.

[05:56] Diego Ramos: We can configure request-level retention policies and strip PII before persisting, and can route sensitive jobs to a private deployment to ensure no retention. We'll document options.

[06:15] Omar Hassan: Back to benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us to run meaningful tests?

[06:21] Priya Nair: Sample prompt sets, labeled dev set (for extraction metrics), representative payload sizes, and expected QPS patterns. Also a list of languages and a few long-article examples.

[06:38] Samir Patel: We can export a 200-example dev set (English/Spanish/German) and a traffic trace for the busiest day. Will that be enough?

[06:45] Diego Ramos: Yes — for the POC benchmark we prefer 200-500 labeled examples plus 50 long-form cases. We'll use your traffic trace to simulate concurrency and burst.

[07:00] Lena Ortiz: Timeline — we want to make a decision in 4-6 weeks. POC should fit into that window.

[07:08] Maya Chen: Typical POC cadence: week 0 (alignment and infra prep), week 1-2 (benchmarks and initial eval across shortlist), week 3 (tune prompts/RAG, run longer tests), week 4 (final eval + presentation). If you want domain fine-tune or on-prem validation that'll add 2-4 weeks.

[07:35] Priya Nair: We'll propose a 4-week baseline POC with two optional extensions: domain fine-tune and Private deployment validation.

[07:45] Diego Ramos: Bench plan specifics — we'll run each model at both FP16 and quantized 4-bit where supported, measure p95 latency for 512 and 2k sequences, throughput at your target concurrency, and quality metrics on your labeled set. We'll also run a hallucination/citation check for the synth flows.

[08:10] Samir Patel: On hardware, what infra do you need for the 40B models? We don't want a huge bill.

[08:15] Diego Ramos: For Falcon-40B you'll want at least A100-ish or equivalent. For the 13B/7B family we can use more cost-effective GPUs (A10/RTX 6000 or even T4s for inference with batching). For the POC Redwood can spin up Dedicated instances for the bench and provide cost estimates.

[08:38] Lena Ortiz: If the 40B shows big quality gains for our domain, we might accept the infra cost, but prefer to see the numbers.

[08:45] Maya Chen: We'll present a cost/quality chart for each model profile so you can make an informed tradeoff.

[08:50] Omar Hassan: Any red flags on hallucinations from open models in biomed?

[08:55] Priya Nair: Open models vary. Some hallucinate more on citations. That's why we pair models with retrieval and citation-checking heuristics. For POC we'll include a retrieval layer prototype and measure citation correctness rate.

[09:12] Diego Ramos: Also we'll run a small human evaluation rubric focusing on factuality and citation correctness. That usually surfaces hallucination patterns quickly.

[09:25] Ruth Kim: Regarding SSO/SSO: we need SAML and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC. Also will Redwood support audit export to our SIEM?

[09:34] Maya Chen: Yes — SAML/SCIM and audit export are supported. We'll include sample configs in the security pack.

[09:44] Lena Ortiz: Great. Anything else on data residency? We operate in EU and US.

[09:50] Samir Patel: Some of our data must stay in EU region; can Redwood route requests to region-specific infra?

[09:56] Diego Ramos: Yes, smart routing by region is supported; for Private we can pin region or run on-prem. We'll note region routing in the SOW.

[10:08] Maya Chen: OK quick recap and next steps. Recap: Halia will provide labeled dev set (200+ examples), traffic trace, and infra diagram by 2026-05-18. Redwood will send POC SOW and pricing by 2026-05-17, security pack by 2026-05-18, and benchmark harness ready by 2026-05-22. We'll schedule the benchmark run week of 2026-05-25 and a follow-up to review results on 2026-06-02. Did I miss anything?

[10:37] Lena Ortiz: That captures it. One note: include per-language success thresholds in the SOW — English >=0.78 F1, Spanish >=0.7, German >=0.68 as tentative.

[10:52] Maya Chen: Noted, we'll add those thresholds.

[11:00] Samir Patel: I'll also include the cloud account info for sandbox and a point of contact for infra.

[11:07] Ruth Kim: I'll circulate our compliance questionnaire this afternoon.

[11:12] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any final questions?

[11:15] Omar Hassan: No, thanks everyone.

[11:18] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and SOW.

End of meeting.
